newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower due to dollar shortage.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower due to dollar shortage.

text.p: The won closed lower against the U.S. currency in a day of widely fluctuating trading on Friday as tight dollar positions pushed the dollars up, dealers said.

"The market continues its rebound in reaction to central bank's intervention last week, which had soaked up a lot of dollars," said a foreign bank dealer. "Many dealers now prefer to go long, and the consensus sparked a stop-loss dollar buying."
The won ended at 890.40, compared with Thursday's close of 889.20. After opening at 890.00, it hit another monthly low of 890.60.
"Many believed the market is in short on the dollars. But they agreed the dollar is in a downward trend in the long run," said a local bank dealer.

Expected inflows of foreign funds for equity investment in Seoul bourse and advanced dollar selling in forward trading by the Housing and Commerical Bank would boost the local currency next week. Dealers forecast a 888-892 range next week.
Friday's trading volume was estimated at $1.59 billion.
Dealers forecast Monday's mid-rate would be pegged at 890.00 against 889.00 today.
